description: US GAAP EXPLAINED — Book 1 is a practical guide to understanding the foundations of U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (US GAAP) and how they are applied in real-world financial reporting. Stop memorizing accounting rules without understanding how they work. U.S. GAAP can seem overwhelming. Hundreds of accounting requirements address revenue, assets, liabilities, financial statements, leases, taxes, impairment, and countless other transactions. The real challenge is not simply knowing individual rules—it is knowing how to identify the right guidance, analyze a transaction, and turn that analysis into a defensible accounting conclusion. This book provides the foundation you need to do exactly that. Designed for accounting students, accountants, CPA candidates, finance professionals, controllers, business owners, and professionals working with U.S. financial reporting , Book 1 explains the core concepts behind US GAAP in a practical and structured way. title: US GAAP EXPLAINED: A Practical Guide to U.S. Accounting Standards - Book 2: Assets, Leases
description: US GAAP EXPLAINED: A Practical Guide to U.S. Accounting Standards — Book 2 continues the series with more advanced accounting topics involving assets, leases, financial instruments, and income taxes. Building on the foundational concepts introduced in Book 1, this practical guide helps readers understand important areas of U.S. GAAP that frequently require careful recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure. The book is designed for accounting students, professionals, finance professionals, business owners, and readers who want a practical understanding of U.S. accounting standards without having to navigate the material as a collection of disconnected technical rules. Book 2 covers: • Accounting for major asset categories • Leases and the core principles of ASC 842 • Lease classification, recognition, measurement, and presentation • Financial instruments and related accounting considerations • Investments and financial assets • Fair value concepts and measurement • Debt and other financial obligations • Income taxes and the fundamentals of ASC 740 • Deferred tax assets and liabilities • Practical financial reporting considerations The focus is on understanding the accounting logic behind the standards and how those principles affect financial statements. US GAAP EXPLAINED is designed to be practical, structured, and accessible while maintaining a professional accounting perspective. If Book 1 provides the foundation, Book 2 moves into the asset, lease, financial instrument, and tax topics that accountants and finance professionals encounter in more advanced financial reporting. title: US GAAP EXPLAINED: A Practical Guide to U.S. Accounting Standards - Book 3: Equity, Foreig
description: US GAAP EXPLAINED — Book 3 is a practical guide to important areas of U.S. financial reporting involving equity, ownership, foreign operations, acquisitions, and consolidation. As companies grow, expand internationally, acquire other businesses, compensate employees with equity, or operate through multiple legal entities, financial reporting becomes increasingly complex. These situations require more than memorizing rules. Accountants must understand the underlying economics, identify the applicable U.S. GAAP guidance, and determine the appropriate recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure. Building on the foundations established in Books 1 and 2, Book 3 focuses on five important areas: Stock-Based Compensation — ASC 718 Equity awards, vesting conditions, fair value, modifications, tax effects, classification, and financial statement presentation. Provisions and Contingencies Litigation, warranties, guarantees, environmental obligations, commitments, loss recognition, and related disclosures. Foreign Currency Functional currency, foreign currency transactions, remeasurement, translation, highly inflationary economies, and foreign operations. Business Combinations — ASC 805 Acquisition accounting, the accounting acquirer, acquisition date, consideration transferred, identifiable assets and liabilities, goodwill, and noncontrolling interests. Consolidated Financial Statements Control, variable interest entities, intercompany transactions, noncontrolling interests, changes in ownership, and loss of control. Throughout the book, practical examples, calculations, simplified journal entries, financial statement effects, common mistakes, and reporting considerations connect U.S. GAAP guidance with real-world accounting decisions. title: US GAAP EXPLAINED: A Practical Guide to U.S. Accounting Standards - Book 4: Financial Repo
description: US GAAP EXPLAINED: A Practical Guide to U.S. Accounting Standards — Book 4 completes the four-book series by LAFP Consulting with a practical guide to financial reporting, earnings per share, subsequent events, related-party transactions, and financial statement disclosures. Designed for accountants, finance professionals, controllers, auditors, CPA candidates, students, and international professionals working with U.S. companies, this volume combines practical explanations, examples, common mistakes, and review checklists. WHAT YOU WILL LEARN Chapter 16 — Cash Flow Statements (ASC 230) Understand operating, investing, and financing cash flows, the relationship between cash flow and net income, and how to assess liquidity and cash generation. Chapter 17 — Earnings Per Share (ASC 260) Explore basic and diluted EPS, weighted-average shares outstanding, and the effects of potentially dilutive securities. Chapter 18 — Subsequent Events (ASC 855) Learn how to evaluate events occurring after the balance sheet date and determine their potential accounting and disclosure implications. Chapter 19 — Related Parties (ASC 850) Identify related-party relationships and understand the reporting considerations for transactions involving owners, management, affiliates, and other connected entities. Chapter 20 — Financial Statement Disclosures Review key disclosure topics, including accounting policies, estimates, risks, contingencies, income taxes, fair value, commitments, and subsequent events. A PRACTICAL APPROACH TO US GAAP This book explains how accounting standards work together to support consistent, transparent, and useful financial reporting. It also discusses selected differences between U.S. GAAP and IFRS, helping readers understand different approaches to financial reporting.

title: GAAP Guidebook: 2026 Edition
description: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) are used as the basis for financial reporting. The original GAAP documents span thousands of pages, and so are difficult to research. The GAAP Guidebook solves this problem by condensing GAAP into a single volume. This book describes the key elements of each topic, how accounting information is disclosed, and where to look in the FASB Codification source documents for additional information. The text contains hundreds of practical examples that show how to apply GAAP to real-world situations, as well as sample journal entries and usage tips.
